chapter: Alcohol, Paris and the hit record
title: Hearing loss and high pitches
summary: His hearing loss means he cannot hear high pitches, such as muted trumpet or flute.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Did you ever find that your early difficulties with not being able to hear the spoken word well stood in the way of being able to hear the things you wanted to hear musically?

No. No because it wasn't so much not hearing the spoken word, it's just the point of knowing if you're speaking to me and then concentrating on your saying it -- something to me. You know, because I -- I don't hear high pitches. I can't hear it. That's why you never hear me trying to play high on a flute; I don't -- I can't hear that.
Really? Yeah, I always wondered about that.
I can't hear it. Like, to me it's just pffffff, you know. So that's.
Could you hear Dizzy when he was playing up high?
Yeah. [scatting] I hear that. But in mute, I can't hear it.
